title: Session provenance and metric actuation canvas
content:
Context: working canvas to connect session provenance (how requests relate across microcalls, KV cache, prefix-warmth) to actionable metric definitions and dashboard widgets. Goal: produce a compact set of metrics + traces that operators can use to (a) detect regressions in user-facing latency/quality, (b) decide fast mitigations (fallbacks, model routing, burst throttles), and (c) measure cost impact of mitigations. This is intentionally practical — treat as an ops playbook sketch and experiment ledger.

Why this exists
- Observability noise is high: investigators lack a reliable starting point that ties a single session to the SLI and the relevant trace spans.
- We need a smaller, instrumentable surface that is both low-query-cost and high-signal for common failure modes (cold KV, prefix mismatch, quantized model fallbacks).

Key terms (operational definitions for this doc)
- Session provenance: the minimal set of IDs and span anchors required to rehydrate a user request end-to-end (request_id, session_id, model_variant, kv_warmth_bucket, routing_policy).
- Metric actuation: the mapping from a metric breach to a recommended operator action (e.g., throttle -> increase batch timeout; cold-cache spikes -> enqueue prewarm job).
- Trace anchor: a short span name and tag set used as the primary link for dashboards (e.g., span=tokenize; tag=kvcache:miss_rate>threshold).

Desired outcomes
1) A standard session provenance header added to all front-door spans and propagated to model-sidecar spans.
2) A compact SLI set (3–6 metrics) per model family that feed a lightweight incident starter dashboard.
3) A runbook mapping each metric breach to 1–2 playbook actions and the minimum trace slices to collect.

Compact SLI candidate list (draft)
- user-ttft (time-to-first-token, p50/p95) — front-door to model-first-token span. Use p95 for alerts; p50 for release signals.
- tail-token-latency (p99 token generation subspan) — helps catch slow-token kernels.
- kv-prefetch-hit-rate (session-windowed) — fraction of sessions where kv was warm for first N tokens.
- routing-fallback-rate (per-customer) — percent requests hitting fallback model variant.
- cost-per-request-adjusted (tokens * effective rate) — approximate allocation for billing-awareness.
- perplexity-drift-proxy (sampled quality metric from rolling prompt-set) — opt-in for models where we can compute quick quality probes.

Trace anchors and labels to standardize
- frontdoor.request (tags: request_id, session_id, client_tier)
- tokenize.subspan (tags: token_count, prompt_length)
- model.exec (tags: model_name, model_variant, gpu_type, quantized=true/false)
- kv.access (tags: kvcache_status=hit|miss|evicted, kv_warmth_bucket=hot|warm|cold)
- routing.decide (tags: policy, reason=fallback|overload|explicit_pin)

Dashboard composition (operator-first, minimal cost)
- Top row: global SLI tiles (user-ttft p95, tail-token-latency p99, routing-fallback-rate, kv-prefetch-hit-rate)
- Middle: cohort slices (by model_variant, region, client_tier) with sparkline 48h and small table showing delta vs baseline 
- Bottom: sample trace list (5 most recent session IDs matching alert criteria) with links to trace UI and raw prompt replay (sanitized)
- Isolation: each tile should have a pre-bound quick-filter: session_id / request_id so operator can open trace from tile.

Metric actuation matrix (example rows)
- kv-prefetch-hit-rate drops > 10% (5m) -> Action: trigger prewarm for affected model_variant; temporary routing to warm-only pool; notify infra if persistent >30m. Trace slices: kv.access spans for session window.
- user-ttft p95 increased by >30% -> Action: switch to lower-latency model_variant with routing-fallback; increase batching threshold for background traffic. Trace slices: frontdoor.request + model.exec.
- routing-fallback-rate > 5% for premium clients -> Action: immediate rollback of recent model rollout; open incident. Trace slices: routing.decide + model.exec + request metadata.

Investigation template (quickcard for ops)
1) Fetch top SLI tile + time window.
2) Apply cohort filters (model_variant, region, client_tier).
3) Grab sample session_id from bottom panel -> open trace and prompt replay.
4) Check kv.access spans and kv_warmth_bucket. If cold: check prewarm queue, recent deployment, and cache eviction events.
5) If model side: check model.exec spans for GPU queueing and quantization markers. If fallback correlated, inspect routing.decide reason.
6) Escalate with these artifacts: session_id, p95 delta, top 3 trace spans (names+durations), link to PR/rollout.

Open questions / TODOs
- Decide cardinality limits for request_id propagation. We want session-level IDs but must avoid unbounded cardinality in metrics. Proposal: hash(session_id) -> 8 chars for dashboards; full id only in traces.
- Sampling policy for perplexity-drift-proxy: how much sample budget can we afford without impacting production tokens?
- Ownership: which team owns the kv-prefetch-hit-rate metric? (suggest infra-models + obs).

Next 90d experiments (tracked)
- Experiment A (2 weeks): Add kv_warmth_bucket tag to frontdoor and model.exec spans for top 3 models; validate dashboard slice correlation. Owner: Marcus.
- Experiment B (4 weeks): Build incident starter dashboard with session_id quick-link; measure mean time to remediation vs baseline. Owner: Priya.
- Experiment C (8 weeks): Implement metric actuation webhooks for 2 playbook actions (prewarm trigger, routing pin). Owner: Alex.

Notes to self
- Keep dashboard query budget bounded: avoid per-request tables; use session-window aggregation and sampling.
- Sketch a lightweight SDK change for adding the session provenance header into envoy/filter chain.

Appendix: short snippet of example span tags (for engineers to copy)
- request_id: "r_64f8a3b2"
- session_id: "s_3b2f9ef"
- kvcache_status: "miss"
- kv_warmth_bucket: "cold"
- model_variant: "rw-v2-small-q4f16"

If you want to iterate: add quick comments inline and ping #obs-infra. Prioritize experiments A and B for Q1 shipping cadence.
